scope: Bounded read-only native-source, patch and retained-test review. No provider/media/network requests, model calls, downloads, imports of the model stack, source edits or test reruns.

findings.finding: The native video branch can follow additional_urls with extract_info even when _type is video. The first patch rejected unresolved URL and playlist types but left this separate dispatch path open.
findings.correction: Nonempty additional_urls and additional_entries now join the existing multiple-video rejection before transfer; two new regression cases require no download.
findings.scope: No such field was observed in the hosted Dailymotion incident. This is a native contract correction, not an attribution of that incident.
findings.minimal_change_verified: Removing only the added metadata guard terms reconstructs the initial reviewed app hash; removing exactly two new test rows reconstructs the initial 18-case test hash.

verified_contracts.reuse: The same object returned by one application-level extract_info(video_url, download=False) call passes duration, declared-size and single-video validation, then is supplied to process_ie_result(info, download=True). Native download([url]) performs a fresh extraction, so replacing it removes that explicit duplicate call.
verified_contracts.native_route: With accepted resolved-video metadata, the inspected API dispatches to normal process_video_result and process_info using the same YoutubeDL instance/options. Unresolved URL, url_transparent, playlist, multi_video, other non-video types and nonempty additional URL/entry metadata are rejected before transfer.
verified_contracts.initial_extraction_scope: This is one application-level extraction, not one HTTP request. The initial native extractor may resolve its own metadata references. No claim forbids ordinary manifest/fragment/transfer requests.
verified_contracts.validation_and_limits: Canonical source selection, 2-hour duration rejection, declared/approximate input-size rejection, max_filesize transport cap, accepted output suffixes, missing-file error and actual final file-size check remain unchanged.
verified_contracts.transport: Format selection, workdir output template, noplaylist, socket timeout, retries, no-overwrite behavior, YouTube JS-runtime selection and explicit system-certificate opt-in remain unchanged. No alternate endpoint, credential use or new retry loop was introduced.
verified_contracts.error_and_cleanup: Readable validation errors remain specific. Native acquisition/transfer exceptions retain the public access message and original cause. The existing guarded-worker finally path still removes audio intermediates; a failed-transfer regression asserts unrelated files survive.
verified_contracts.native_test_quality: The native contract case executes installed yt-dlp result processing with an owned fake extractor and intercepted media transfer. urlopen raises on network attempts, the extractor asserts it is invoked once, and selected id/title/duration/format/media URL are checked. It is a real native processing contract test, not a live-provider or actual transfer test.
verified_contracts.production_scope: AST comparison confirms every other module-level statement/function is unchanged from HEAD; only _download_source_audio differs.

remaining_limits: The live Dailymotion no-video-formats incident remains a failure. Existing logs do not identify whether the old first or second extraction failed, and this offline change does not prove provider availability is restored.
The historical ASR anchor failure remains unchanged: retained sentence starts before its frozen containment window. No decoder, timing window or speech output changes belong to this patch.
The native API contract was inspected against exact yt-dlp 2026.11.23 bytes. Normal future dependency validation still applies; no broad compatibility or provider-success claim is made.
